label: D2 late-episode, a2 after a2 S2 unrewarded (or a2 S1 rewarded)
terms: (phase == D2) * (action == 1) * np.exp(ep_trial/25) ;; (phase == D2) * last_is("a2 S2 u") * np.exp(ep_trial/25) ;; (phase == D2) * (action == 2) * last_is("a2 S2 u") * np.exp(ep_trial/25) ;; (phase == D2) * last_is("a2 S1 r") * np.exp(ep_trial/25) ;; (phase == D2) * (action == 2) * (state == 2) * np.exp(ep_trial/25) ;; (phase == D2) * (action == 2) * (prev_reward == 0) * np.exp(ep_trial/25)
explanation: Active only at D2 (zero at D1/GO), and its size grows roughly exponentially with trial in the episode (scale ~25 trials; timing alone R^2 0.21). On top of timing, it is largest when the agent has just chosen a2 and the previous trial was a2 -> S2 unrewarded (strongest term), and it is also raised after a2 -> S1 rewarded. Both of those previous outcomes are evidence that S2 is bad. Reaching S2 after a2 raises it a little more. Choosing a1 on this trial pushes it to near zero. All the terms are scaled by exp(ep_trial/25), so the late-episode growth multiplies with the history effects; that is why these 6 terms beat the additive all-cue ceiling of 0.34. Policy uncertainty (exp(-|choice|)) and a1 S2 u add <0.01. The trial before last adds little. Dev R^2 beyond timing 0.52, test 0.51. All terms are observed at D2 (no future variables).

issues: The biggest misses are window-boundary artifacts, not a gap in the explanation. The worst-fit dev windows are mostly the first trial of the window (rel -3, previous trial unknown, so last_is is 0): the agent chose a2, reached S2 common, prev_reward is 0, and the feature reads 1.5-2.2 against a prediction of about 0.2. Adding (phase==D2)*exp(ep_trial/25)*(prev_action==-1)*(action==2)*(prev_reward==0) raises test R^2 beyond timing from 0.515 to 0.545. The agent itself sees its previous trial; the window just cuts it off.
The scale-25 exponential is well supported. Without it the same terms reach test 0.27; scale 15 gives 0.46 and scale 40 gives 0.50, so the multiplicative late-episode claim checks out.

The history claims check out on test. Keeping only (action==1), a2-after-'a2 S2 u' and a2-after-'a2 S1 r' gives 0.497. Dropping the 'a2 S1 r' term gives 0.485. Fitted weights: a2 S2 u +0.010 plus +0.019 more when a2 is chosen; a2 S1 r +0.010; a1 -0.005; a2 reaching S2 only +0.002, which really is 'a little'.
The explanation leaves out that the (action==2)*(prev_reward==0) term gets a negative weight (-0.003). It acts as a correction to the a2 S2 u terms, not as a 'non-reward raises it' effect.

The 'evidence that S2 is bad' framing overreaches slightly. 'a1 S2 u' (rare unrewarded) is also evidence that S2 is bad, yet adding it gains only about 0.003. The effect is specific to a2 history, which the label states correctly.

Remaining systematic errors are small next to the activation's std of 0.144: D2 after a1 S2 r over-predicted by -0.041 and D2 after a2 S2 r by -0.036 (both from the shared a2/S2 terms), and D2 after a1 S2 u under-predicted by +0.05, falling to +0.019 with that term added. A 2-back a2-unrewarded term adds less than 0.01, which agrees with 'the trial before last adds little'.
